skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Guides agents through the inference.sh belt CLI for discovering and running cloud AI apps, including image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and Twitter/X workflows.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh cloud AI apps from the belt CLI.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms critical installer risk from multiple curl-to-shell examples and high-risk handling of local file paths that can be uploaded to cloud apps. Most API-key and documentation-link matches are false positives, but the skill still performs external CLI operations, remote app execution, and account automation. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with verified package-manager or checksum-first install steps, and require explicit approval before installation.
Avoid command substitution from a remote manifest. Pin release URLs and verify checksums or signatures before installing binaries.
Require explicit consent for every local path, and warn before using parent-directory, home-directory, media, or document paths.
Require confirmation before posting, uploading media, sending messages, following, liking, or retweeting through Twitter/X apps.

remediation.issue: Executable installation into the user PATH
remediation.suggestion: Document the install location, provide uninstall commands, and do not move unverified downloads into PATH directories.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps with belt
content.value_statement: AI app workflows often require many separate provider tools. This skill guides Codex, Claude, and Claude Code through belt commands for discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and authenticate the belt CLI.
Lists commands to browse, search, filter, and inspect public apps.
Provides examples for image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and Twitter/X apps.
Explains local file inputs, automatic uploads, and task status checks.
Documents samples, inline inputs, async tasks, results, and shell completions.
limitations: Requires the external belt CLI and an inference.sh account.
Commands can send prompts, media, and local files to cloud services.
Provider availability, pricing, and model names can change outside the skill.
The pipe-to-shell installer path needs safer verification guidance.

use_cases.title: Prototype media workflows
use_cases.description: Find and run cloud apps for images, videos, audio, and 3D assets from one CLI flow.

use_cases.title: Compare model providers
use_cases.description: Inspect public app schemas and run LLM, search, or generation tasks through provider-specific apps.

use_cases.title: Track long tasks
use_cases.description: Submit longer cloud jobs, keep task identifiers, and retrieve generated outputs when they complete.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to find inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the best options and explain when to use each one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to inspect the input requirements for a video generation app and prepare a safe run plan before executing it.

prompt_templates.title: Run and track a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to run a long video task without waiting, save the task identifier, and check the result later.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-step workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to design a workflow that searches for source material, generates media, and tracks every cloud task with explicit approvals.

output_examples.input: Find a cloud app for generating a product image.
output_examples.output: The skill returns candidate image apps, summarizes each schema, and recommends the safest app to run for the requested asset.

output_examples.input: Run a long video generation job and check it later.
output_examples.output: The skill submits the task, records the task identifier, and later reports the task status and available output links.

output_examples.input: Use a local image as input for an upscaling workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill warns that the file will upload to a cloud app, asks for confirmation, then uses the selected file path.

best_practices: Ask for explicit approval before installing the CLI or running remote app commands.
Confirm every local file path before upload, especially parent or home directory paths.
Use task identifiers and app schemas to keep cloud runs reproducible.
anti_patterns: Do not run the pipe-to-shell installer without verifying the source and checksum.
Do not upload local media, audio, or documents without user confirmation.
Do not post, follow, like, retweet, or send messages through X/Twitter without explicit consent.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents use the belt CLI to discover, run, and track inference.sh cloud AI apps.

faq.question: Does it require an external account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require the belt CLI, an inference.sh login, and available account credits or permissions.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The referenced CLI can automatically upload local paths when an app input accepts files.

faq.question: Can it automate Twitter or X actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents app examples for posting, media uploads, follows, likes, retweets, and messages.

faq.question: Is installation fully safe by default?
faq.answer: No. The documented pipe-to-shell installer should be replaced with verified download steps and user approval.

faq.question: Which agent tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
